item.title: Nikko Autumn Foliage: Maple-Lined Roads and Waterfalls — Guide
item.description: Nikko is one of Japan’s premier autumn foliage destinations, its mountainous terrain and elevation range meaning colour changes progress gradually from the highlands down to the town over several weeks each October and November. The winding, hairpin-heavy Irohazaka road, connecting central Nikko to the Okunikko highlands, is famous for spectacular views of maple-covered valleys, while Kegon Falls and the grounds around Toshogu shrine offer equally striking, if more accessible, autumn scenery.
